title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 444
paragraphs: Then the Lacedemonians prepared a force and made an expedition to Samos, in repayment of former services, as the Samians say, because the Samians had first helped them with ships against the Messenians. But the Lacedemonians say they made the expedition not so much from a desire to help the Samians at their request, as to take vengeance on their own behalf for the robbery of the mixing-bowl they had been carrying as a gift to Croesus, and of the corslet which Amasis, king of Egypt, had sent as a gift to them; for the Samians had carried off the corslet as well, in the year before they took the bowl. The corslet was of linen with many figures woven into it and embroidered with gold and cotton, and each thread of this corslet is worthy of admiration, for though it is itself fine, it has in it three hundred and sixty fibers, all plainly visible. Another such as this, moreover, is the one Amasis dedicated as an offering to Athene at Lindos.
